title: Alma Har’el’s Family Drama ‘Wet’ Heading To TIFF Market With 193; A-List Cast Circling
full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Jason Statham Buyers Ponder Whether Amazon Leak Caused ‘Mutiny’ At Box Office: “There’s Been Plenty Of Finger-Pointing” ‘Lord Of The Rings’ Producer Lines Up New “Large-Scale” Fantasy Movie ‘Wars Of The Drakons’ AI Sci-Fi Series ‘Kira’ Heads To MIPCOM For Ex Machina & K5, First Look Images View All August 29, 2026 7:17am Alma Har'el Getty Honey Boy director Alma Har’el’s next project Wet is heading to the TIFF market with Patrick Wachsberger’s 193 and is attracting what could be a killer cast. News of the project broke online last month via Page Six who reported that Oscar winner Javier Bardem was in talks. Bardem remains in early talks for the project, and we can reveal that Mission Impossible and Dune star Rebecca Ferguson, Heated Rivalry ‘s Connor Storrie and Marty Supreme breakout Odessa A’zion are also in very early discussions. No deals are done and as is often the case with market packages, there’s a chance they change or don’t come together at all, but buyers are likely to spark to this cast. Related Stories Festivals 'Krux' Trailer: Toronto-Bound WWII Drama Captures True Story Of Disintegration Of Order In German Village Casting Odette Annable Leads Cast In Horror 'Postmortem'; Sublimity Launches Sales For TIFF As First Look Revealed Little has been revealed about the plot but we can confirm it’s an original script from Har’el and Christian Stangeby that is said to be in the vein of HBO’s Succession and the Oscar nominated Palme d’Or winner Triangle of Sadness . If the script gets close to those projects, buyers will likely be in thrall. Watch on Deadline Wachsberger’s 193 is handling international sales. Fifth Season is due to finance and produce alongside Chris Leggett, Riva Marker, and Har’el. The hope is to shoot in Spain early next year. Har’el’s last feature was her debut, Honey Boy , which was written by and starred Shia LaBeouf. The 2019 film, which was picked up by Amazon, garnered largely positive notices and played at festivals including Sundance and TIFF. Har’el was in development on an adaptation of dystopian science-fiction novel Mockingbird for Searchlight. In the meantime, she has also directed TV. Bardem had great write-ups for his turn in Spanish movie The Beloved at Cannes and U.S. distributor Kino Lorber is aiming for a fifth Oscar nomination for the actor. Reps and 193 declined to comment. title: ‘Paranormal Activity’ Broadway Review: Stage Adaptation Of Film Franchise Is A Frightfully Good Time
full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Alex Winter Bringing Arthur Miller’s ‘Incident At Vichy’ Revival To Off Broadway Next Year Amid Growing Galliano Backlash, Met Gala Mulls Date Change – Report James Walsh Dies: Tony-Winning Broadway Producer Of ‘The Heidi Chronicles’ & ‘I’m Not Rappaport’ Was 89 View All August 29, 2026 7:00am Travis A. Knight, Cher Álvarez, 'Paranormal Activity' Matthew Murphy There are plenty of laughs in Paranormal Activity , a play that just might be Broadway ‘s scariest horror story ever, but they’re not the lighthearted jolly chuckles of, say, Titanique or the gut-bucket guffaws of Oh, Mary! No, the laughs in Levi Holloway ‘s chiller are more along the lines of those recalled from sharing a movie theater showing The Exorcist : Relief-fueled roars spurred on by the embarrassment of having just shrieked out loud like Jamie Lee Curtis in Halloween . The movie references, of course, are intentional: Holloway’s Paranormal Activity, unerringly directed by Felix Barrett (the Punchdrunk founder and artistic director behind the popular immersive Sleep No More ) and starring two Broadway newcomers who by all rights should by now be overnight stars, is based (in spirit, as it were, if not plot) on the durable Paramount Pictures film franchise of the same name. Related Stories Obituaries James Walsh Dies: Tony-Winning Broadway Producer Of 'The Heidi Chronicles' & 'I'm Not Rappaport' Was 89 News Tim Curry Remembered By 'Rocky Horror Show' Playwright Richard O'Brien & The Broadway Revival And while the production borrows just about every worthwhile horror movie trope and scare tactic ever committed to film, this Paranormal Activity feels entirely (and idiosyncratically) of the stage , as if Holloway and Barrett worked some voodoo magic to have us all forget that we’ve ever so much as heard of, much less seen, slamming doors, impossible shadows, glitchy television sets with minds of their own and lamps that flicker like so much lightning. This play uses ’em all – to just about perfect effect – along with only-in-the-theater elements like stage lighting and sound designs that amp up the scare volume (literally) to shattering results (and not just on your eardrums, though that too.) Watch on Deadline Ditching the films’ plotlines for something new, if, obviously, related, Paranormal Activity follows young American couple Lou ( Cher Álvarez ) and James ( Travis A. Knight ) who have recently relocated from Chicago – where some strange, vaguely described things involving “lost time” and black-outs bedeviled poor Lou. So right from the start we have a time-honored set up: A young wife who might be haunted or maybe just unbalanced, and won’t be entirely trusted by the men in her life one way or the other. That’s a trope as socially relevant today as it was when Gaslight (a film that gets name-checked here) owned it, and Rosemary’s Baby perfected it and Let’s Scare Jessica To Death took it to the drive-in. Let the man pretend to be the hero. We know the truth. Well, we think we do, anyway. Playwright Holloway has all sorts of tricks up his many sleeves, turning misdirection (visual, narrative, aural or otherwise) into a symphony of look-here! no look-there! shifts. There’s a shocking moment early on in which writing, directing, acting, the illusions by Chris Fisher, the lighting by Anna Watson and sound design by Gareth Fry come together so seamlessly and impactfully that the audience response is a mix of serious what- was -that gasps and very loud shrieks. Followed by that embarrassed laughter, naturally enough. The play opens on Fly Davis’ two-tiered set – a largish but comfy and lived-in London flat, bedrooms upstairs and always on view so we see what the couple downstairs doesn’t – with the sound of a podcast filling the theater. The podcaster is a thick-accented medium, of sorts, who reminds us that houses aren’t haunted, people are. Remember that. Álvarez in ‘Paranormal Activity’ Matthew Murphy The anticipated spine-tingles begin almost immediately, when buzzy light fixtures and TV static make nuisances of themselves, and dazed Lou is wont to stare into a middle-distance at a presence only she can sense. James, though loving and well-intentioned, can’t help but show his skepticism, repeatedly (and blithely unaware of his condescension) asking if his wife remembered to take her meds today. Audiences don’t need to fret about some prolonged is-she-or-isn’t-she red herring though: Soon enough, James is met with incontrovertible proof that, no indeed, they are most definitely not alone. Even the podcast medium, making a house call (perhaps the only truly unbelievable moment in a tale that by all rights should be stocked with them), freaks out when she comes face-to-face with something she probably never really believed could exist. To give more away would be to spoil the good, scary fun that unspools over the two-hour running time, a running time, by the way, that is filled with long, tense moments of quiet anticipation expertly broken by very loud blasts of everything from rock music to slamming doors, burglar alarms, doorbells, the proverbial bumps in the night and an intensely unsettling, nearly incomprehensible voice from the ether. Old, carefully guarded secrets are revealed, shames are exposed, blame is tossed and no one is safe from the past, the predictions or one another (especially when the other isn’t all he or she appears to be). Newcomers Álvarez and Knight couldn’t be better in their newlywed roles, convincing in their giddy love scenes, their casual affections, their unwanted suspicions and, most of all, their terror at whatever is lurking in the air and in their souls. In supporting roles, Eva Kaminsky as the gorgeously-named spiritualist Etheline Cotgrave does well to keep us on our toes, and Shannon Cochran, as James’ Southern Christian evangelical mom, is both funny and suitably creepy whether she’s moralizing in person or via long-distance video screen chats. The mom’s name, not so incidentally, is Carolanne, just a tiny space away from “they’re heeere” Carol Anne of Poltergeist . Yes, a bit on the nose, but who could begrudge Holloway for indulging in some fun for himself? Having perfected this whole stage fright business since his underrated 2019 outing Grey House, which now seems like a practice run, the playwright, along with his director, cast and creative and technical teams, have gifted us a smashingly diverting entertainment to kick off the Broadway fall season with a big, loud bang. Or several. Title: Paranormal Activity Venue: Broadway’s August Wilson Theatre Written By: Levi Holloway Directed By: Felix Barrett Cast: Cher Álvarez, Travis A. title: Alex Winter Bringing Arthur Miller’s ‘Incident At Vichy’ Revival To Off Broadway Next Year
full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Alex Winter Bringing Arthur Miller’s ‘Incident At Vichy’ Revival To Off Broadway Next Year Amid Growing Galliano Backlash, Met Gala Mulls Date Change – Report James Walsh Dies: Tony-Winning Broadway Producer Of ‘The Heidi Chronicles’ & ‘I’m Not Rappaport’ Was 89 View All August 29, 2026 6:00am L-R: Alex Winter, Kanika Asavari Vaish, Ben Natan Rick Wenner/Courtesy EXCLUSIVE: Alex Winter , who costarred with his old Bill & Ted partner Keanu Reeves last year in the Broadway revival of Waiting For Godot , will return to the New York stage next year in a Small Boat Productions Off Broadway revival of Arthur Miller’s 1964 play Incident at Vichy . Winter will both star in and produce the one-act play, expected to open in spring 2027. Kanika Asavari Vaish will direct, with additional casting, production dates and venue to be announced . Related Stories News Acclaimed Pulitzer Finalist ‘Here There Are Blueberries’ To Open On Broadway This Fall News ‘The Fantasticks’ Broadway Cast Announced: Maxim Chlumecky, Nathan Levy, Ruthie Ann Miles, Zane Phillips & Others To Star Also producing are Ben Natan, AJ Liu and Connie Tavel. Mix and Match Productions will serve as the General Manager. “I am honored and thrilled to be working with such a visionary team to bring this brilliant, riveting and timely work of Arthur Miller’s to audiences Off Broadway”, Winter said in a statement. Watch on Deadline First staged on Broadway in 1964 with Harold Clurman directing a cast that included Hal Holbrook and Tony Lo Bianco, Incident at Vichy was set in 1942 and focused on a group of men undergoing “racial inspection” by German military officers and Vichy French police detained in Vichy, France. The revival will feature a cast with actors of different races and genders who will play the characters as written by Miller. According to Small Boat Productions, “ Incident at Vichy in the 21st Century will strip away the lavish, realistic set and period costumes and instead focus on what is happening and to whom. This is not a play about one moment trapped in time; rather, it is a play about an ongoing catastrophe of indifference and inaction in the face of atrocity. What happened in Vichy, France happened across all of Europe, it happened in Vietnam and Indonesia, and is happening now across Ukraine, Lebanon, Gaza, Iran, and Minneapolis.” Said director Vaish, “It’s a dream come true to work with Small Boat Productions on the urgent, heart-racing cautionary tale that is Incident at Vichy . Arthur Miller’s enduring impact rivals Shakespeare’s, with a consistently socially conscious body of work that challenged power structures and society’s complicity during his time and still reaches modern audiences with the horrors of today. I am especially excited to be championing marginalized voices on an Off Broadway stage to the hungry, attentive, New York audience.” “I’m so thrilled that the Arthur Miller estate has entrusted Small Boat to bring this story back to New York City”, said producer Natan. “Arthur Miller is the great American playwright, and Small Boat wants to champion the full breadth of his work. We have an amazing team of theater artists from all corners who are coming together to make this production truly special to honor Miller’s legacy and the power of this play.” Spidey Winning Again; ‘Coyote Vs. title: Amid Growing Galliano Backlash, Met Gala Mulls Date Change – Report
full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Alex Winter Bringing Arthur Miller’s ‘Incident At Vichy’ Revival To Off Broadway Next Year Amid Growing Galliano Backlash, Met Gala Mulls Date Change – Report James Walsh Dies: Tony-Winning Broadway Producer Of ‘The Heidi Chronicles’ & ‘I’m Not Rappaport’ Was 89 View All August 29, 2026 5:49am Anna Wintour, John Galliano Getty Amid growing backlash over the Met Gala ‘s choice to honor designer John Galliano at the big event next May, Met trustees and board members are “mulling” whether to reschedule the fundraiser away from the previously announced May 3 date to avoid coinciding with the Holocaust and Heroism Remembrance Day. The possibility of postponing the gala for a week has been raised in a New York Times report on the increasing Galliano backlash: The accomplished British fashion designer was convicted of a hate crime by a French court in 2011 for making public antisemitic outbursts, and earlier this month The Times reported that Vogue’s global editorial director and a Met trustee Anna Wintour , Galliano and other Gala organizers had been meeting over the course of the past year with “influential rabbis and Jewish leaders” in New York City “to get their thoughts on the potential issues with next year’s planned fashion extravaganza — a show dedicated to Galliano’s work — and perhaps their blessing for it.” Related Stories Culture John Galliano Announced As Subject Of 2027 Met Gala And Costume Institute Exhibition Culture Met Gala 2026 Photos: Best Of The Red Carpet From Beyoncé, Madonna, Rihanna, Sabrina Carpenter And Teyana Taylor To Janelle Monáe Now a second Times report notes that concern over the choice of honoree has only become more troublesome since that first article was published a month ago. According to an article by Vanessa Friedman, the Times’ fashion director and chief fashion critic, and Times’ Style writer Jacob Bernstein appearing today on the news site, Met trustees and board members “have been scrambling to do damage control” over the Galliano selection. Watch on Deadline “For starters,” Friedman and Bernstein report, “they are mulling whether to move the date of the next Met Gala from its usual slot, the first Monday in May, to the week after. In 2027, Yom HaShoah, also known as Holocaust and Heroism Remembrance Day, will fall on the scheduled party date.” Met Gala officials, including trustee Anna Wintour, who is a noted champion of Galliano, have not publicly addressed the possibility of a gala date change. Vogue magazine, the de facto official publication of record for the gala, still lists, as of today, May 3 as the gala date. Today’s Times article details the opposition to Galliano’s selection that has grown among Jewish leaders in recent days. According to the Times, “Donors have contacted Met executives and threatened to rescind gifts to the museum if the exhibition moves forward as planned. They have reached out to Wintour, Andrew Bolton, the curator of the Costume Institute, and Max Hollein, the museum’s director.” For example, the paper notes, Julie Menin, the speaker of the City Council, and one of the most senior Jewish officials in city government, called the museum’s decision to highlight Galliano’s career “a serious mistake” in a letter she sent on Thursday to Hollein, Bolton and Wintour. “Our cultural institutions, particularly those that receive funding from the City of New York, have a responsibility to demonstrate that hatred and bigotry carry consequences,” Menin wrote in the letter, which was shared with The New York Times by a museum official. “Words matter, and whom we choose to elevate is a direct statement of our values and what we are willing to tolerate.” According to The Times, Menin wasn’t the only newly outspoken critic of the honoree. Arne Glimcher, described by the paper as an “art world titan,” recently sent an email critical of the plan to Hollein and David Breslin, a Met curator, stating, “I don’t think you have considered the cost of this action and its reverberations to come,” adding that he and his wife “are seriously reconsidering other works that have been earmarked from our collection to the Met in our wills.” And Jill Kargman, a longtime member of the patron group Friends of the Costume Institute, announced she is stepping down from her role due to the Galliano project. In a statement to the Times yesterday, museum director Hollein said, “The Met has no tolerance for antisemitism, racism or prejudice of any kind. We are in close consultation with Jewish leaders and other stakeholders, and we take the concerns we’ve heard very seriously.” He added that Met leadership “is developing a thoughtful plan for next year’s exhibition and gala that meets the moral and ethical standards set by the museum.” Spidey Winning Again; ‘Coyote Vs. title: Inside ‘The Great British Bake Off’ Bun Fight: How Sky & Love Productions Came To Blows Over The UK’s Biggest Cooking Series
full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Inside ‘The Great British Bake Off’ Bun Fight: How Sky & Love Productions Came To Blows Over The UK’s Biggest Cooking Series Edinburgh TV Festival Diary: Farewell To The Great City; YouTube Takeover; Channel 4’s Next Content Chief & Paramount Mischief ‘The Pitt’ & ‘The Celebrity Traitors’ Win Prizes At Edinburgh TV Festival Awards View All August 29, 2026 1:07am 'The Great British Bake Off' Season 17 Channel 4/Love Productions EXCLUSIVE : In an op-ed during the Edinburgh TV Festival this week, Sky ’s content chief Cecile Frot-Coutaz extolled the virtues of UK public service broadcasting as the Comcast -owned company finalizes its takeover of ITV . “Our ambition is to keep investing in brilliant British storytelling for generations to come,” she intoned in Broadcast . But away from the polished words, Sky has been accused of imperilling one of the UK’s biggest public service broadcasting success stories: The Great British Bake Off . In a battle at odds with Bake Off ’s wholesome charm, Sky and Frot-Coutaz find themselves defending furious complaints from producers central to the success of Channel 4 ’s cooking series. Producers who dedicated much of their careers to Love Productions, the respected company wholly acquired by Sky in 2020. Related Stories News Edinburgh TV Festival Diary: Farewell To The Great City; YouTube Takeover; Channel 4's Next Content Chief & Paramount Mischief News International Insider: The Final Edinburgh... Or Is It?; Int'l Oscar Race Begins To say this situation is unusual is an understatement. In the polite world of British television, it is vanishingly rare for producers to go on record with their grievances against powerful networks and their executives, let alone sue them. But such is the strength of feeling, former Love managing director Letty Kavanagh has launched twin lawsuits against Sky for wrongful dismissal and unpaid severance, as revealed by Deadline this month . Two others have complained to Sky citing similar concerns: Kieran Smith, Bake Off ’s former executive producer, and a third unnamed individual, who remains employed by Love. Watch on Deadline Paul Hollywood has judged every season of ‘Bake Off’ Deadline has reviewed Kavanagh’s legal filings and spoken to people familiar with the dispute to understand how relations curdled. After an 18-year career at Love, Kavanagh claims she was fired for complaining that Sky’s bid to poach Bake Off from Channel 4 in 2025 was improper, mismanaged, and damaged relations with a key customer. She believes her experience shows that Sky does not have the best interests of public service broadcasting in its DNA. In other words, it serves as an unhappy harbinger for ITV ahead of its £1.6 billion ($2.2B) sale. Sky strongly rejects allegations of impropriety and mismanagement, and has said it will robustly defend its position during the legal proceedings. Sky insiders attribute the Bake Off battle to differences of opinion about the show’s future, which led to a breakdown in professional relations that has nothing to do with its proposed ITV takeover. Gibson Dunn, an external law firm, investigated and dismissed Love’s complaints. Sky can also point to the irrefutable outcome of the Bake Off disagreement: That the show stayed free-to-air on Channel 4 and remains in rude health. Project Rise Love Productions founders Richard McKerrow and Anna Beattie built a culture that valued creative independence, meaning relations with Sky were not always straightforward. There has long been a feeling in Osterley that Love bosses struggled to come to terms with surrendering their ownership to Sky in 2020. Low-level disquiet erupted into open hostilities in early 2025, when Frot-Coutaz launched Project Rise, the codename for Sky’s efforts to snaffle Bake Off from Channel 4. Channel 4 has been home to Bake Off (known as The Great British Baking Show on Netflix) since acquiring the series from the BBC in 2016. Love executives wanted to maintain the status quo. Indeed, Kavanagh, with the blessing of Sky, had in 2024 negotiated terms for a new Channel 4 contract, including an output deal that would have enabled Love to create new shows for the network. Cecile Frot-Coutaz So when Sky said it wanted to explore switching Bake Off , it went down like a sunken soufflé at Love, where producers had serious misgivings about the show fading into irrelevance behind Sky’s paywall. These misgivings were compounded by Sky’s alleged approach to Project Rise. In her employment tribunal lawsuit, Kavanagh claims that Frot-Coutaz “intermeddled” in Bake Off contract talks with Channel 4 between January 2025 and November 2025, “undermining goodwill” at Love’s most important customer. This is denied by Sky sources, who say it was appropriate for Frot-Coutaz to explore options for Bake Off and that relations with Channel 4 remain in fine fettle. People close to Kavanagh allege that Frot-Coutaz signalled her intention to take Bake Off , then left Channel 4 in limbo for months, sparking alarm among the broadcaster’s most senior executives, who began preparing for life without their biggest franchise. Channel 4 declined to comment. Meanwhile, Sky had a plan for Bake Off that would involve ditching spin-off series, including the professionals and kids’ versions. Love’s leaders were aghast. “Sky was prepared to make hundreds of people unemployed at the drop of a hat,” recalls one person. Then Frot-Coutaz suddenly abandoned Project Rise. Love was unclear on the reasons for her volte-face, but speculated that Sky had failed to convince Bake Off stars like Paul Hollywood to make the switch. People close to Kavanagh also allege that senior Sky content executives, including unscripted chief Philip Edgar-Jones, were uncertain that Bake Off was a good fit for the network. Sky does not recognize this characterization of Edgar-Jones’ position. Sky negotiated Bake Off ’s renewal directly with Channel 4 in October 2025, meaning Kavanagh was only told about the deal after it was done. In her lawsuit, she alleges that Sky’s renewal was “materially less advantageous” than the one she negotiated in 2024. Some estimate that it wiped millions of pounds off the value of the contract and potential side deals, such as the U.S. licensing agreement with Netflix. Channel 4 insiders are certainly not unhappy with the outcome. Kavanagh was furious and repeatedly made her concerns clear to her superiors at Sky. Within days, she was fired and marched out of the building in November 2025. Nine months on, she has filed two UK lawsuits — one in an employment court and a second at the High Court — that chronicle at least four grievances. Kavanagh’s Lawsuits Kavanagh alleges that Sky’s pursuit of Bake Off was a conflict of interest because the broadcaster was privy to contractual arrangements with Channel 4. Sources close to the producer allege that “ethical walls” between Love and Sky’s content team were smashed down in 2024, when Frot-Coutaz’s Sky Studios empire was expanded to include unscripted commissioning. In her employment tribunal filing, Kavanagh alleges that Sky commercial chief Helen Northrop “agreed” that “this was an issue.” Letty Kavanagh Sky disputes the conflict of interest allegation, arguing that there is no legal basis for the claim because it wholly owned Love and Bake Off . Sky denies that Northrop ever concurred with Kavanagh’s concerns. Senior figures at the pay-TV giant are genuinely perplexed by Kavanagh’s claim, and they argue that taking Bake Off in-house would not have been without precedent. ITV poached The Voice from the BBC soon after ITV Studios acquired Talpa in 2015. Kavanagh also alleges that Sky imposed changes on Love’s annual accounts to create a flattering financial picture by booking margin on incomplete projects early. Sky refutes the accusation, attributing the changes to updated accounting practices introduced in 2023 at Comcast’s request. Kavanagh further accuses Sky of sex discrimination over the termination of her contract and, in a separate High Court lawsuit, claims she is owed £755,752 ($1 million) in severance payments. Sky denies the accusations and maintains that it has no financial liability to Kavanagh. Sky says Kavanagh’s concerns about Project Rise and accountancy practices were investigated when she and colleagues made whistleblowing complaints. Gibson Dunn, an external law firm, was engaged to review the allegations. Kavanagh and Kieran Smith were interviewed, and their complaints were not substantiated. They have since questioned the rigour of the investigation, claiming they were not provided with a terms of reference or given access to documents on which they relied. Sky stands by the findings. It has since installed new management at Love and then subsequently agreed to sell the company to ITV Studios for £200 million as part of its ITV takeover. A Sky spokesperson says: “As the sole owner of Love Productions, Sky has every incentive to protect and enhance the value of The Great British Bake Off . We have invested in the show and its long-term future for more than a decade and continue to do so today. “As with any long-running programme, when an agreement approaches renewal, it is natural and appropriate to consider the options for its future. The Great British Bake Off continues to be enjoyed by millions of viewers, and Sky agreed a new deal which keeps it on Channel 4 and free-to-air. “The allegations were subject to a comprehensive investigation by leading external counsel and were not substantiated. We deny the claims against Sky and will vigorously defend our position in the ongoing legal proceedings.” Where Kavanagh believes she is raising the alarm about a “cutthroat” American culture that’s coming for ITV, Sky sees an effort to embarrass the company into a settlement. Meanwhile, Bake Off returns to Channel 4 for Season 17 next month, welcoming new judge Nigella Lawson to the tent. That this almost did not happen could be a bun fight that goes all the way to court. Monsoon rains repeatedly destroy their shelter, and the city offers them little beyond hostility and indifference. It is the father’s stories about the boy’s late mother – her boldness and her refusal to let go of playfulness even as she navigated the city and the natural world – that allow the son to see himself as more than a victim, and give him the will to dance among the ruins as she did and rebuild his life. title: Shailene Woodley Was Crushed When She Found Out Her Scenes in ‘Amazing Spider-Man 2’ Were Cut: The Role of Mary Jane Was ‘My Dream’

Woodley, in a recent interview as part of the “SAG-AFTRA Foundation Conversations” series with actors about their craft, revealed that she found out a year after filming for “The Amazing Spider-Man 2” that she would not appear in the movie, which was released in theaters in May 2014. Mary Jane was my favorite character growing up. So, when I got it, I was like, ‘This is so exciting.’” Woodley said she filmed “like three scenes together, me and Andrew Garfield. title: Olivia Rodrigo’s Inaugural Daisy Chain Fields Will Be a Showing of Unity — Even for Photographers
full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All August 28, 2026 9:12pm Olivia Rodrigo performs during an exclusive Billions Club Live show to celebrate the partnership between Spotify and FC Barcelona before El Clásico on May 8, 2026. (Photo by Xavi Torrent/Getty Images for Spotify) On the eve of the Olivia Rodrigo ‘s Daisy Chain Fields , the superstar singer turned up Friday afternoon in Santa Monica where she revealed that her inaugural female forward music festival would be donating $10 million to a variety of causes. “Daisy Chain Fields was created to celebrate the power of what can happen when we come together to support one another,” she said while joined by executives from 10 nonprofits to pump the massive showing of support for their women-centric causes. That support is expected to be spread across all corners at Great Park in Irvine, Calif. on Saturday — both in front of and behind the camera. The Hollywood Reporter hears that Rodrigo was passionate about lifting up as many women as possible throughout the event that it will largely feature female photographers capturing the stage and ancillary activations. (That includes trans, nonbinary or gender nonconforming individuals.) It is also known that while it was a goal of the event, Rodrigo and organizers mounted the entire affair with an inclusionary rather than exclusionary mission, so it’s not a hard-and-fast rule that every photographer be a woman. “Good vibes” were most important. Related Stories Music Olivia Rodrigo's Daisy Chain Fields Raises $10 Million for Women-Focused Nonprofits Music Gladys Knight Announces She'll Partake in "Fewer Performances" Amid "Next Stage" of Career and Life Still, it would be quite a feat to pull off. Back in 2018, a group of 82 women climbed the steps of the Palais during the Cannes Film Festival to shine a spotlight on the lack of female directors who have had a chance to screen their films at the iconic gathering. At the time, a female photographer pointed out what a powerful moment it was despite the fact that it was captured by hundreds of male photographers, and only a handful of women photographers. Behind the scenes, photography and videography remains a field largely dominated by men. “It’s ironic women stood in solidarity and had a moment of silence while being shot by 500 male photographers objectifying the hell out of them,” the photographer explained at the time. That won’t be the case Saturday. Daisy Chain Fields , presented by Rodrigo, will feature performances by the singer alongside Bikini Kill, Chappell Roan, Devon Again, Die Spitz, Doechii, Eli, Garbage, Mitski, Not For Radio, Quiet Light, Rachel Cinouriri, Santigold and The Breeders, with special guests Karen O, Sarah MacLachlan and Stevie Nicks. They were able to raise $10 million through sponsors and the fact that the artists set to hit the stage are doing so for free. As THR reported today, the money will be dispersed to Baby2Baby, Black Mamas Matter Alliance, Center for Reproductive Rights, FreeFrom, Jhpiego, John Hopkins Center for Indigenous Health, National Domestic Workers Alliance, National Institute for Reproductive Health, National Women’s Law Center and Planned Parenthood. title: Jackie Glass, ‘Swift Justice’ Host, Dies at 70
full_text: Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All August 28, 2026 8:52pm Jackie Glass John Locher-Pool/Getty Images Judge Jackie Glass, host of the syndicated legal television show Swift Justice , has died. She was 70. Glass’ daughter Rachel Wolfson announced her death on Facebook . She died Friday in Las Vegas, according to TMZ . “Rip my rock, I don’t know how I’ll do this life without you, I love you so much mommy Jackie Glass, I’ll see you again someday,” Wolfson wrote, while also sharing a follow-up post with a series of images alongside her mother. Glass, a previous long-standing Clark County judge, took over hosting Swift Justice in 2011, serving as the successor to Nancy Grace, who first led the show. She went into the series with a prominent presence, having served as the judge who sentenced O.J. Simpson to 33 years in prison for armed-robbery at a Las Vegas hotel in 2008. He was later granted parole in 2017, and died in 2024 at age 76 after a battle with prostate cancer. At the time, when it was announced she was taking the reigns for Grace, executive producer John Terenzio said he was “excited to introduce viewers to another true original Judge Jackie Glass — we are confident our viewers will enthusiastically embrace her.” Before she was elected to the judgeship in Clark County in 2003, she spent 18 years as a lawyer in private practice, including 12 years at Wolfson & Glass, a firm she founded with her husband Steve Wolfson . Glass is survived by her husband and two daughters. THR

title: Naomi Osaka Debuts a Luxury Accessories Brand at Uncharted’s Fame to Fortune Summit in the Hamptons
full_text: Aug 28, 2026 7:44pm PT Naomi Osaka Debuts a Luxury Accessories Brand at Uncharted’s Fame to Fortune Summit in the Hamptons By Corbin Bolies Plus Icon Corbin Bolies Latest Naomi Osaka Debuts a Luxury Accessories Brand at Uncharted’s Fame to Fortune Summit in the Hamptons 11 hours ago ‘The View’ Host Sunny Hostin Licenses Her Likeness to AI Studio: ‘A New Art Form’ 2 days ago Peter Cullen, Voice of Optimus Prime in ‘Transformers,’ Dies at 85 2 days ago See All Getty Images Tennis champion Naomi Osaka has for years made the tennis court a runway, with her Nike outfits often paired with pieces made in collaboration with designers such as Hana Yagi and Robert Wun. Her next staple piece: one she’s designed herself. Such is the brand of luxury leather goods Osaka unveiled Friday at the Fame to Fortune Summit , a daylong conference organized by the affluent community-building organization Uncharted that aimed to connect celebrities flirting with potential business ideas with investors eager to fund them. Osaka showcased a prototype of one of her handbag creations during a chat alongside her business partner Mike Cherman, the founder of the Los Angeles streetwear line Chinatown Market, in which she called the brand her “biggest dream” outside of tennis. Related Stories Dolly Parton Skips Dollywood Ride Opening Amid Ongoing Health Problems: 'My Nashville Doctor Has Kinda Clipped My Wings' Bill Maher Delivers Lamest Dolly Parton Tribute Yet “Being a really good tennis player has given me a lot of amazing opportunities to invest and also just to surround myself with some really great people and I feel like that’s gotten me to this point where I want to create my own thing,” Osaka told Fortune‘s executive editorial director Diane Brady during the fireside chat, which also served as a pitch to potential investors in the crowd. “It’s something that I want to pour all my energy into because I believe in it too with all my heart.” Popular on Variety Osaka’s conversation, in between her practice rounds at this year’s U.S. Open, was one of the keynote panels during the daylong confab, held at the sprawling Southampton, New York, shoreside estate of Uncharted co-founder Michael Loeb. Variety was one of the conference’s five media partners alongside Yahoo, Fortune, the New York Stock Exchange and Culture. Over the course of the morning, guests filtered into the estate’s backyard deck, which included several food stations (including a Mexican spread by the Hamptons native Crispy Taco Co.), a coffee station with Kenyan coffee farmer Margaret Nyamumbo’s brand Kahawa, an opportunity to test drive Cadillac’s CELESTIQ sedan and a mixture of cocktails and mocktails for a crowd where an 11 a.m. Friday morning libation is less an end-of-week reward and more an expectation. Attendees mingling around the house’s pool ranged from finance professionals who flocked from across the country to names familiar among media and entertainment circles, including one-time CNN chief Chris Licht chatting in a small gaggle and former child actor Skai Jackson of the Disney Channel’s “Jessie” introducing herself to a new crowd. Jackson, 24, say s that while the summit was the first time she’d attended an event so heavily focused on business, it tapped into her entrepreneurial spirit as she batted around three different venture ideas (all of which she declined to share with Variety ). “I feel like you always have to be really ready to start something up — it’s definitely such a huge commitment,” she says. “You have to be all just in with it and full throttle. So now that I have my baby, my baby is old enough, I feel like, OK, I can finally get back into doing what I want to do.” It’s a goal Loeb and his Uncharted co-founder Justin Barth hoped the Fame to Fortune Summit would achieve for its attendees, with the two using their opening remarks to implore the hundreds of guests under the setup dining tent to break away from the communities they came with and network with someone new to help capitalize on their celebrity as they think about new businesses. “I don’t think anybody is going to walk out of here today with a $100 million business or a billion-dollar business, but you’re going to come out with ideas, and also some of the enablers that are going to help you do it,” Loeb said. Though that’s not to say all went according to plan. The temperamental weather conditions stemming from a looming storm had staff quickly setting up plastic coverings around the tent throughout Osaka’s conversation to protect from the oncoming rain. And, after an amusing crowdwork-focused performance by “foodie magician” Josh Beckerman, the keynote conversation that started the day’s programming was not with scheduled headliner VaynerMedia CEO Gary Vaynerchuk, who dropped out, but instead with Kevin Durant agent and business partner Rich Kleiman, who spoke about navigating the music and sports industries and his time working with artists including Jay-Z, Solange and, of course, Durant. Kleiman tells Variety that he didn’t really know much about the event when he was approached, but Loeb’s involvement and more time to network among the Hamptons crowd helped spur his participation. “I’m not trying to come offstage and close a deal,” he says. “It’s fascinating to always meet people and see how what we’re working on connects with people. I think we all live in our bubbles … The more you get out of the world, the more you’re outside around people — that’s the best news of what’s happening. title: Sara Bareilles Sings About Loss — and It’s Our Gain — in the Beautifully Bittersweet ‘Good Grief’: Album Review
full_text: Aug 28, 2026 6:46pm PT Sara Bareilles Sings About Loss — and It’s Our Gain — in the Beautifully Bittersweet ‘Good Grief’: Album Review Bareilles is mourning a few things — the deaths of close friends, dreams of easy fertility, assumptions of female autonomy, the American dream — but the music soars, more often than not. By Chris Willman Plus Icon Chris Willman Senior Music Writer and Chief Music Critic ChrisWillman Latest Sara Bareilles Sings About Loss — and It’s Our Gain — in the Beautifully Bittersweet ‘Good Grief’: Album Review 12 hours ago Zak Starkey and the Who Have Kissed and Made Up, as Rehearsal Reunion Is Revealed 13 hours ago David Byrne’s Dazzling Tour Being Turned Into a Film by ‘Brutalist’ Director Brady Corbet, Shooting in 70mm 2 days ago See All Epic Records Well, just how good can grief be? That’s a question raised by Sara Bareilles ‘ “Good Grief,” which, true to its promissory title, deals primarily with loss and death and the kind of tough stuff that folks in a marketing meeting might suggest slightly downplaying when one is releasing one’s first studio album in seven years. If that focus sounds like it could make for a slog, Bareilles — who was prompted to go down this path by the death of her decades-long best friend — is very much into finding ways to celebrate as well as mourn, or at least actively explore how those two polarizing impulses might intersect. But apart from that, there’s the matter of just how awfully spirit-lifting her earth-angel mezzo-soprano tends to be, even when backing herself into dark corners before backing her way back out again. All of which is to say: Music lovers could not ask for a better bereavement counselor. Related Stories Dolly Parton Streams Surge on Spotify With 2,320% Increase in the United States Dolly Parton Honored by Kacey Musgraves, Keith Urban, Reba McEntire: 'We Will Always Love Her' Not one to put off dealing with the elephant in the room, she concentrates several of the songs most overtly tied to her friend’s death from cancer in the first third of the album. Counterintuitively, perhaps, this is where some of the most joyful-sounding material is found too. Bareilles starts off with “Home,” which approaches the subject matter from a different angle, paraphrasing bits of a conversation she saw Stephen Colbert and Anderson Cooper share on television about their own experiences with grief, and how for many of us it gets emotionally brushed under the family dinner table: “I was taught to bury with the dead / The presence of my grief / I see it now, but didn’t then / That silence is a thief / It made strangers out of friends / Robbed me of saving graces offered in unlikely places.” Popular on Variety The second number, “Just Kids,” is where she begins to bring her own experiences with loss in, going in completely on her late BFF, college bestie and former tour manager Chad Joseph, finding some wryness in the details — “You never got to get married and I hate where you’re buried” — yet a weird exultation in writing about him in real time. In a meta moment, she describes herself singing the song she’s writing about him as a voice mail she’s driven to put down as a voice mail, in public: “Out on the street / Singing in the phone / They’re looking at me / There was a time / That I might have cared / But this one’s for my best friend so let ’em stare.” If this were one of her past or future Broadway musicals — say, a sequel to “Waitress” where Jenna has to plan a funeral — it would be the 11 o’clock number. By track 3, the Aaron Dessner-co-produced “Still Crying,” she’s hovering over a deathbed: “Pray, pray to someone I used to know / I request a rescue / Tell Him that he moves too slow.” But it’s not arranged as the somber ballad you might expect, but as a waltz-tempo ode to emotional exhaustion that sounds weirdly romantic, almost like an old-fashioned doo-wop tune, but with tearlessness replacing true love as the ideal end game of all this striving. (Bareilles cites Roy Orbison as the reference point in interviews.) At this point it’s pretty clear that “Good Grief” will never be a grind to get through, however tough the stuff it deals with is, and with the album just getting started, and a lot of potential showstoppers scattered throughout in a variety of moods and styles, the clock will not get run out too exhaustingly or early. There is a song dealing movingly with IVF struggles Bareilles has been open about, “Ladies in Line.” (Sondheim might appreciate this strange echo of the “Company” line.) She offers two numbers that touch on the grief Americans might feel about current sociopolitical currents: the dramatic, ominously percussive “Hands Off My Body,” first premiered in concert a couple of years back (“No I’m not gonna choke on a thank you / To a god I don’t pray to / Your holiness haunts me”), and “Heartland,” a defiantly hopeful patriotic ballad sung partly from the point of view of the Statue of Liberty. There’s even a devastating breakup ballad, “Say Leave,” although Bareilles is fairly recently (and apparently happily) wed; she’s not above borrowing from friends’ romantic experience to find a bonus way here to break some hearts, just in case the death stuff didn’t get you. But fans who follow her on social media, where she’s discussed mental health struggles, will sense she’s writing more out of her own life again with “Nervous Breakdown.” The title sounds like it could be a last, harrowing straw, but it’s actually a track that breaks the noble mood as a purely fun, semi-comical jazz shuffle that delves into high anxiety over the ironic comfort of a cabaret-style stand-up-bass-and-piano combo. “I’m having a nervous breakdown / Just me myself and I / You, you’re not invited!” she warns, through what sure sounds like a smile. But of course, “Good Grief” is an invitation, to commiserate and put a dent in the cycles of misery — be they related to death, love or America, even — through the sharing of voices, starting with Bareilles’ sweetly uplifting guide vocal. And all that, as someone once said, baked in a beautiful pie. title: California Tries Offering Hollywood New Perks to Make Up for Catch in $750 Million Incentive Program
full_text: × Skip to main content By Katie Kilkenny Plus Icon Katie Kilkenny Enterprise Reporter, TV & Labor katiekilkenny7 Follow Sign Up View All August 28, 2026 6:23pm A view of the California State Capitol on August 19, 2025 in Sacramento, California. Justin Sullivan/Getty Images After failing to secure an exemption for the entertainment industry, stakeholders have made a last-minute proposal to mitigate the impact of California‘s new business tax credit regulations on Hollywood. State Assemblymember Rick Chavez Zbur and Senator Ben Allen on Friday introduced AB/SB 186, which if passed would exempt indie projects from the state‘s new business tax credit caps and allow all productions with state tax credits to monetize more of their refunds, faster. “Last year, we took action to get families back to work and jumpstart the State’s film and television industry,” Senator Allen said in a statement. “However, we’re at risk of losing this momentum, and all the jobs we’ve created over the last year, if we don’t act by the end of the month. I’m grateful for the support from Governor Newsom, Assemblymember Zbur and the legislative leadership to help us find a path forward that will retain California’s status as the global hub of entertainment.” Stakeholders say a state budget bill that was signed into law on June 29 has jeopardized the celebrated increase to California‘s film and television tax credit increase to $750 million in 2025. That 2025 boost to the program, the result of some serious lobbying from Hollywood, more than doubled the amount of funding that could be allocated to giving productions tax relief. But budget bill SB 122 threatened its viability by extending previously temporary caps on the use of business tax credits over $5 million a year. The budget bill also made the ceiling on using credits over $5 million a year, or 70 percent of a taxpayer’s liability, whichever is greater, permanent starting in 2030. The new trailer bill wouldn‘t give major productions a pass from these caps, but it would enhance the perks for productions that choose to monetize a portion of their tax credits rather than put them towards their tax liability. (The ability to monetize a portion of the tax credits is relatively new, having been signed into law in 2025). The bill allows production to monetize 95 percent of their refund, as opposed to the previous 90 percent, and speeds up the collection period from five to two years. The bill additionally would push back the expiration date for credits earned before 2025‘s changes to the program for productions actively shooting in California. Productions recently awarded California tax credits would have 15 years to use them, rather than the previous nine. The trade organization for major studios and streamers, the Motion Picture Association, supports the bill alongside the Entertainment Union Coalition and the Producers Guild of America. The introduction of AB/SB 186 follows a major lobbying campaign from unions and the MPA , as well as a letter-writing campaign from union members, to oppose the inclusion of the entertainment industry in the business tax credit caps. As of August 14, some 350,000 letters had been sent to legislators airing industry members‘ concerns about what the state budget bill could mean for production in the state. While Zbur and Allen‘s bill addresses concerns over productions realizing the full value of their credits, it may not do much to restore trust in policymakers‘ approach to the state‘s film incentives program. Stakeholders have expressed concern that the sudden change to the program implemented this year could scare companies seeking stability and certainty as they make long-term production plans. Now, legislators will have to scramble to pass the bill before the legislative session adjourns on August 31. “I’m pleased that we have identified a path forward that would help protect the progress we’ve made to strengthen California’s film and television industry,” Assemblymember Zbur said in a statement. He added of the bill, “It does not address every challenge facing this highly competitive and mobile industry, and there is more work to do in the coming months, but this is an important step toward ensuring film and television remain a cornerstone of California’s economy.” THR

title: Zak Starkey and the Who Have Kissed and Made Up, as Rehearsal Reunion Is Revealed
full_text: Aug 28, 2026 5:43pm PT Zak Starkey and the Who Have Kissed and Made Up, as Rehearsal Reunion Is Revealed By Chris Willman Plus Icon Chris Willman Senior Music Writer and Chief Music Critic ChrisWillman Latest Sara Bareilles Sings About Loss — and It’s Our Gain — in the Beautifully Bittersweet ‘Good Grief’: Album Review 12 hours ago Zak Starkey and the Who Have Kissed and Made Up, as Rehearsal Reunion Is Revealed 13 hours ago David Byrne’s Dazzling Tour Being Turned Into a Film by ‘Brutalist’ Director Brady Corbet, Shooting in 70mm 2 days ago See All Getty Images Apparently the deep and much-talked-about rift between the Who and former (and future?) drummer Zak Starkey was not quite a hell-freezes-over situation after all. Starkey, who was famously revealed to have been unceremoniously handed his walking orders in April 2025, is now back with Roger Daltrey and Pete Townshend … or at least he has rehearsed with them in advance of expected future dates. Both Daltrey and Starkey have made public statements announcing and confirming the somewhat surprising musical reconciliation. Representatives for both Starkey and the Who confirmed to Variety that the respective statements are accurate. Related Stories Dolly Parton, 1946-2026, In Appreciation: A Life of Many Colors Dolly Parton's Musical Will Still Open on Broadway 'As Was Dolly's Wish' In a solo gig at the Encore Theater in Las Vegas on Wednesday night, Daltrey informed the audience had recently done a rehearsal with Starkey and “it sounded great,” according to a review of the show the next day in the Las Vegas Journal-Review . Popular on Variety That this was coming direct from Daltrey was especially unexpected, since the singer had been perceived by much of the public as the surviving member who was most aggrieved by Starkey,’s playing or behavior, although Daltrey went on in interviews to suggest that he was being made into a fall guy for a somewhat unpopular decision that was not his alone. And then, sure enough, Starkey — who had played with the band for 30 years and made it abundantly clear that he would welcome being invited back — confirmed that what Daltrey had said was true. On social media. Starkey, who is the son of Ringo Starr, posted a screenshot of the relevant paragraph from the Las Vegas newspaper review, and then added his caption: “Nice one Rog x. Lookin forward to tearin it up with The Who again..The rehearsal was great.. I don’t think we’ve ever rehearsed as tough as that .. usually we drink tea and talk about what time we’re going home!” Then Starkey made a more formal statement, given to Variety , further establishing his zeal for the reunion: “We rehearsed for an afternoon and were absolutely on fire,” the drummer wrote. “I’m so happy to be back playing the music I love with people I love. It’s good to be home.” If you’re asking yourself “Didn’t the Who do a farewell tour last year?,” the answer is, that was a U.S. farewell tour the band wrapped up last October, with Starkey having gotten the boot before it started. But that didn’t mean the group wasn’t still prepared to make one last swing around other parts of the world, or even to do one-off concerts in the States. “It’s not over by any means,” Daltrey told the Arizona Republic about the Who, while publicizing his solo tour. “It’s just that was the last tour of America for the Who.” The singer mentioned to that interviewer that the group had recently done a rehearsal to make sure they were properly ready to do a farewell tour in Europe, without mentioning at that time that Starkey had taken part in the rehearsal, if indeed it is just one rehearsal that has taken place so far. The exact reasons for Starkey’s dismissal have been clouded, with some deciding that it must be due to an on-stage dispute between Daltrey and Starkey over their lack of being in sync during the band’s first-ever performance of “The Song is Over,”, while intimates of the group suggested that the real reasons for a split had to do with other factors. In interview after he was let go, Starkey insisted that he didn’t understand what had happened, even while pointing out that he was still in regular contact with both Daltrey and Townshend. In July 2025, Starkey did an interview with Variety in which he cheekily declared, “I’m the most famous drummer on welfare.” He said that when he was sacked, he had been asked to say that it was his decision to quit, which was not acceptable for him. ““I’m not a rock star and they are,, but I’m not gonna let people… make me look fucking bad and them look good because they want me to lie,” he told Variety then. “I wouldn’t do it… and then when they did it, I just threw ‘em under the fucking bus because it was bullshit. And then my dad stepped up for me, and that was the greatest thing in the world.” He elaborated: “I didn’t really enjoy being treated like that at all, because (Daltrey) is my friend , but he was wrong. And Roger is one of them guys that, once he’s made his mind up, there ain’t going back. And I couldn’t believe the amount of support that happened. And then, how many times do you get fired twice?” Of reconciliation prospects, Starkey then said, “I feel like anything could happen, but if it doesn’t, I’m cool with it, man. … The weirdest thing was, the day before I got sacked the last time, I’d done an interview with the Sunday Times and I said, “’t’s a vocation, man, being in the Who — it’s not a job. It’s like being a nun, or a nurse.’ And 12 hours later after that, I was fired. It’s so fucked up. But actually, it’s so funny, isn’t it? That’s what’s great about it. It’s funny as well as fucking insane. … If it doesn’t come back together, then it doesn’t come back together. But wow, what a great 29 years, man. I’d like to make it 30. title: Jelly Roll Clarifies Political Views, Regrets Not Taking “Opportunity to Speak Up” at Grammys
full_text: × Skip to main content By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All August 28, 2026 5:42pm Jelly Roll at the 2026 Grammys. Kevin Winter/Getty Images for The Recording Academy Jelly Roll is ready to speak out about his political beliefs. Months after he declined to get political at the 2026 Grammys , the singer-songwriter opened up about his views on Thursday’s Jimmy Kimmel Live! , which he’s been guest hosting this week while Kimmel’s been on his summer hiatus. Earlier in the week, he made a number of jokes about Donald Trump in his monologue, which sparked backlash from some conservatives. Thursday night, he shed more light on his political views. Related Stories TV Jelly Roll Takes Jabs at Donald Trump While Guest Hosting 'Jimmy Kimmel Live!' Music Trump Orders Flags to Fly at Half-Staff in Wake of Dolly Parton's Death: "The World Loves You" “It is funny that before this week everybody thought I was MAGA. And now they think I’m some sort of liberal snowflake,” he said. “Hosting Jimmy Kimmel’s show doesn’t mean I have all of Jimmy Kimmel’s politics . Sure, I lean left on some things, but like most folks I’m pretty down the middle.” He added, “I am a Christian. I am a country music singer. I’m a farmer. I’m a bow hunter. And most of the things I eat, I prefer to get with a stick and a string. That’s the truth.” He went on to say that his beliefs are “simple” and that he wants those who are struggling — including a “recovering addict,” a “felon who is trying to change his life” and a “single mama working a double hard for her family”— to feel seen. And he expressed regret for not sharing more about his ideology when he won three Grammys earlier this year. “That night at the Grammys, I had an opportunity to speak up for people who were scared, hurting and felt like nobody was speaking for them. I had a microphone and I didn’t use it the right way,” he said. “So I am going to try to do the right thing right now because human dignity isn’t Republican nor Democrat. Compassion isn’t left wing and mercy isn’t right wing. Pain and healing know no partisanship. Hurting hearts are more important than poll numbers. And there are no boundaries or borders for broken families.” During his acceptance speech for best contemporary country album, Jelly spoke passionately about his faith and urged people to find Jesus. “There was a time in my life, y’all, when I was broken. That’s why I wrote this album. I didn’t think I had a chance y’all,” he said in part. “I was a horrible human.” He reflected on how music and his faith helped him find his way out of the darkness: “I believed that music had the power to change my life and God had the power to change my life.” In closing, he added, “Jesus is for everybody. Jesus is not owned by any one political party. Jesus is Jesus. Anybody can have a relationship with him. I love you Lord.” But backstage he refused to open up about his political beliefs, despite numerous artists condemning ICE onstage that night. “People shouldn’t care to hear my opinion. I’m a dumb redneck,” he said at the time. But he vowed that he would open up about his beliefs eventually. “I have a lot to say about it … and everybody’s going to hear exactly what I have to say about it the most loud and clear way I’ve ever spoken in my life,” he added. Thursday night he called his Grammy wins the “greatest honor” and the fulfillment of a childhood dream. “And immediately after, I was asked to make what I felt at the time was a political stance,” he said. “I was afraid that anything I was going to say was going to be immediately taken as a political statement. And, ironically, by trying so hard not to make a political statement, I became one.” He added, “For the last six months, I’ve watched people decide who I am, what I am, what I believe, what I support and what I don’t support. And I felt that even more this week, just because I told a couple of jokes.” Instead, Jelly said, he should’ve said, “[Jesus] gave us two commandments. ‘Love God with all your heart and love your neighbor as yourself.’ … There wasn’t a political party exemption. It did not require us to know what country you were born in. There wasn’t a sentence afterward that said, ‘Unless you’re afraid of them.’ It just said, ‘Love your neighbor.'” The former convicted felon, who was pardoned in December, said that now that he’s had his right to vote restored, he plans to make his voice heard in the midterm elections this year. He said he “would never be so afraid of being called political again” And he urged people to come together: “We may disagree. We may argue. We may vote completely. But let’s try not to let the couple of things we disagree about forget the hundreds and hundreds of things we have in common.” THR

title: California Lawmakers Settle on Partial Film Carveout From Tax Credit Cap
full_text: Aug 28, 2026 5:32pm PT California Lawmakers Settle on Partial Film Carveout From Tax Credit Cap By Gene Maddaus Plus Icon Gene Maddaus Senior Media Writer @GeneMaddaus Latest California Lawmakers Settle on Partial Film Carveout From Tax Credit Cap 13 hours ago Blake Lively Awarded $400,000 in Attorneys’ Fees in Justin Baldoni Case 3 days ago Rob Bonta Says He’s Open to Paramount Talks if ‘They Put a Lid on Their Lying Leaks’ 4 days ago See All Asilvero via Wikimedia Commons California lawmakers have agreed on a partial carveout for the film and TV industry from a state cap on tax credits. The bill, AB 186, was unveiled on Friday evening. It addresses concerns raised in June by the Motion Picture Association and a coalition of entertainment unions, who argued that the cap threatened to undermine the state’s $750 million tax incentive program. The state budget seeks to stabilize revenues by preventing corporations from claiming more than $5 million a year in tax credits for the next three years. Industry stakeholders argued that the measure had the unintended consequence of hamstringing Hollywood’s recovery by limiting the ability of studios to use state incentives for in-state production. Related Stories CNN Apologizes for Mistakenly Airing Photo of Dolly Parton Impersonator in Report on Late Singer Bill Maher Delivers Lamest Dolly Parton Tribute Yet The MPA and the Entertainment Union Coalition have signed on to the agreement. As Variety reported on Aug. 18, the deal falls short of their request for a complete exemption for film tax credits from the $5 million cap. Popular on Variety Instead, the legislation will accelerate the payback period for studios that elect to refund their credits for cash. Under existing law, studios can choose to get cash back instead of claiming the incentives as a credit against tax liability — but at the cost of a 10% discount, with a payback period of five years. The deal will accelerate that period to just two years and reduce the haircut to 5%. The agreement also fully exempts credits for independent film — which account for 10% of the $750 million program — from the cap. “It meaningfully improves the situation,” said Kathleen Thompson, vice president of tax incentives at Cast & Crew, a production services company. “They threw a bone to both the studios and to independents.” The deal also extends the expiration date of non-refundable tax credits issued prior to 2025 by up to five years. That provision is meant to help studios that are still sitting on millions of dollars of old, unused credits, and were at risk of having them expire after nine years. The bill is authored by Sen. Ben Allen and Assemblyman Rick Chavez Zbur, who also wrote the bill that increased the incentive program to $750 million last year. In a statement, Zbur said that the fix will provide “greater stability and certainty” for production workers. “It does not address every challenge facing this highly competitive and mobile industry, and there is more work to do in the coming months, but this is an important step toward ensuring film and television remain a cornerstone of California’s economy,” Zbur said. The deal is almost identical to an earlier version that circulated in Sacramento last week. A fact sheet accompanying that version said that it would “mitigate some of the impacts” of the tax credit cap. The only significant difference that a provision to make it easier to claim credits against sales tax — which had been sought by studios — was dropped. The compromise is the result of complex negotiations among industry unions, studios, legislative leaders and the office of Gov. Gavin Newsom. State leaders resisted an industry-specific carveout because it would have led to calls for similar consideration for the tech industry. The bill must be approved by both houses by midnight on Monday, and is expected to do so. title: ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ Star Will Forte, Director Celebrate Film Finally Hitting Theaters After Being Shelved by Warner Bros.: “Proof Movies Don’t Just Go Away”
full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All August 28, 2026 4:04pm Lana Condor and Will Forte in 'Coyote vs. Acme.' Courtesy of Warner Bros. Pictures Logo text The time has finally come: Coyote vs. Acme is now playing in theaters. To celebrate the film’s official release day, director Dave Green shared a thank-you letter on social media, writing in part, “COYOTE VS. ACME IS FINALLY, GLORIOUSLY, IN THEATERS NOW. Which means one thing. WE WON. You can go see this movie. In a theater. In your favorite seat. With your favorite snacks. With your favorite people. You can head into a dark room and laugh with strangers. Together. Congratulations to everyone who made this happen.” Coyote vs. Acme , a hybrid live-action and animated movie set in the Looney Tunes universe, follows Wile E. Coyote as he sues the Acme Corporation after its products repeatedly fail him in his pursuit of the Road Runner. The film stars Will Forte , John Cena, Lana Condor, Eric Bauza and Martha Kelly. Related Stories Movies Will Forte Says Glowing Reviews for 'Coyote vs. Acme' "Make It Feel Like You're Not Crazy," Admits "I Felt Gaslit For a While" Movies 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Hits No. 2 on All-Time Domestic Chart, Topping 'Avengers: Endgame' The film’s journey to theaters has been anything but typical. The Hollywood Reporter exclusively reported in November 2023 that Warner Bros . had shelved Coyote vs. Acme after the movie was completed. The project had been in development at the studio for years and was originally intended as an HBO Max streaming original before Warner Bros. ultimately decided not to release it. At the time, Warner Bros. said the decision came as the studio shifted its global strategy to focus on theatrical releases following the relaunch of Warner Bros. Pictures Animation. The studio also planned to take an estimated $30 million tax write-off by shelving the approximately $70 million movie, according to reports. The decision sparked widespread backlash from fans, filmmakers and the film’s stars, who continued to publicly advocate for the movie’s release . In March 2025, Ketchup Entertainment acquired the worldwide distribution rights to Coyote vs. Acme from Warner Bros., giving the film a path to a theatrical release. The deal was reportedly valued at around $50 million. Green went on to explain why the film’s theatrical release is a “victory.” “It’s a record of the cast and crew, post, prep and animation teams who poured so much love and passion into it over years and years,” he wrote. “It’s shared, permanently, with the audience who fought so hard for its survival. Your fight is the reason this film finally made it to the big screen. Thank you @ketchupentertainment for hearing the audience. We’re so grateful that you did.” “This is a celebration, it’s proof that movies don’t just go away. We make work so it can be seen and shared — that’s the whole reason we do what we do. Persistence and resilience have truly won the day. Enjoy Coyote vs. Acme on the big screen. Where it was always meant to be seen!” Green concluded his letter. Forte took to X on Friday to reply to Green’s letter, writing, “Beautifully put, Dave.” He also shared a video thanking people for their efforts to push for the movie’s release and explaining how its messages correlate with the film’s journey. “It’s about hope and determination. It’s about fighting injustice, and it’s about the importance of friendship and the importance of community. And that last one really strikes a chord because we went through some weird times with this movie, and it is only because of the support of the community that we’re here today, seeing this movie,” Forte said. “You guys lifted us up on your shoulders and just fought and fought for this movie. Most of you, without even having seen it. So I am forever thankful, and just want you to know that I’m so excited for you to see this because I think you’re going to see that it was worth the fight.” In THR ‘s profile of Green , published earlier this month, DC Studios co-head James Gunn, who produced the feature and worked on the story, also reflected on Coyote vs. Acme ‘s journey. “Dave was a great guy throughout the ups and downs. He was never overly bitter and negative, although a little bit of bitterness and negativity was understandable in the given circumstances,” he said. “However, I think you see, when people show true character in the face of adversity, the world rises up to meet them. And in this case, it did — Coyote vs. Acme being saved is because of Dave’s character and because he made a great movie too powerful to be buried. And gosh, perseverance is kind of what Wile E. and the movie are all about.” View this post on Instagram THR

title: Shelley Fabares’ Cause of Death Revealed
full_text: × Skip to main content By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All August 28, 2026 4:01pm Shelley Fabares at an Alzheimer's Association event in Beverly Hills in 2012. Jason Merritt/Getty Images for Alzheimer's Association Shelley Fabares’ cause of death has been revealed. The actress, who starred in Coach and The Donna Reed Show among other TV series and films, died Saturday after a brief illness. She was 82. Fabares died of pneumonia, her family revealed Thursday to People and other outlets. She had previously been diagnosed with autoimmune hepatitis. And she had a liver transplant in October 2000 after spending nearly two years on the waiting list to receive one. “To her family and friends, Shelley was a source of love, strength, laughter and comfort,” Fabares’ family said in a statement announcing her death. “She was a devoted wife, cherished stepmother, daughter, sister, niece, aunt, family member and loyal friend whose warmth, generosity, humor and grace made an enduring difference in the lives of everyone who knew her. She had a remarkable ability to make people feel welcomed, valued and cared for.” Related Stories Lifestyle Coach Toasts Elle Fanning and 'Sentimental Value' at San Vicente Bungalows Soiree Lifestyle Jayson Tatum Talks NBA Playoffs, Acting Ambitions and His New Coach Fragrance Campaign Fabares, whose survivors include her husband, M*A*S*H actor Mike Farrell, played wholesome daughter Mary Stone on The Donna Reed Show , which aired from 1958-1966 on ABC. She went on to star opposite Elvis Presley in three movies (1965’s Girl Happy , 1966’s Spinout and 1967’s Clambake ) and star alongside James Caan in the 1971 TV film Brian’s Song . And, during her time on Donna Reed , she recorded a version of “Johnny Angel” that hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in April 1962. She later starred in Coach as the TV newscaster wife of Craig T. Nelson’s college football coach. She earned two Emmy nominations for her role on the ABC comedy, which ran for eight seasons from 1989-1997. Her other credits include roles on the original One Day at a Time in the late ’70s and ’80s, 1976-1977’s The Practice with Danny Thomas, Highcliffe Manor and Forever Fernwood . THR

title: Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Raises $10 Million  for Women-Focused Nonprofits
full_text: × Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All August 28, 2026 3:50pm From left: Fatima Goss Graves, Kelly Sawyer Patricof, Norah Weinstein, Dr. Allyson Bear, Christian LoBue, Olivia Rodrigo, Caren Spruch, Jenn Stowe, Sonya Passi, Madeline Halperin-Robinson, Angela D. Aina and Dr. Melissa Walls at Friday's Daisy Chain Fields press conference. Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Daisy Chain Fields Olivia Rodrigo ‘s Daisy Chain Fields is donating $10 million to its nonprofit partners, the superstar revealed Friday during a press conference ahead of Saturday’s inaugural festival. “Daisy Chain Fields was created to celebrate the power of what can happen when we come together to support one another,” Rodrigo said Friday, flanked by executives from the 10 nonprofits. “The organizations we’ve partnered with are doing incredibly important work every single day in the U.S. and globally. I’m so grateful to every person who bought a ticket, every artist who waived their fee , every sponsor for signing onto a brand new festival and every donation that helped get to $10 million dollars to support women and girls. I can’t wait to see everyone tomorrow.” Related Stories Music Olivia Rodrigo's Inaugural Daisy Chain Fields Will Be a Showing of Unity -- Even for Photographers Music KATSEYE Drops Out of Daisy Chain Fields After Megan Sprains Ankle View this post on Instagram The $10 million will be dispersed across 10 different groups whose missions range from reproductive health advocacy and resources for mothers to support for survivors of gender violence and abuse. The full list of nonprofits are Baby2Baby, Black Mamas Matter Alliance, Center for Reproductive Rights, FreeFrom, Jhpiego, John Hopkins Center for Indigenous Health, National Domestic Workers Alliance, National Institute for Reproductive Health, National Women’s Law Center and Planned Parenthood. Rodrigo first announced Daisy Chain Fields back in June , calling the event “a festival founded on the belief that joy, community and creativity can inspire meaningful change.” Inspired by the Lilith Fair music festivals of the ’90s and 2000s, the festival will feature the likes of Rodrigo, Chappell Roan, Mitski, Doechii, Bikini Kill, the Breeders, Garbage, Eli, Quiet Light, Rachel Chinouriri, Devon Again and Not For Radio. Stevie Nicks, Karen O and Lilith Fair founder Sarah McLachlan are listed as special guests. Katseye was originally on the lineup as well, though the group announced Thursday that they had to pull out after Megan said she sprained her ankle during a rehearsal. “The woman performing tomorrow and those sitting beside me today inspire me so much,” Rodrigo said Friday. “They’ve taught me a lot about how we are all stronger when we come together and support one another. That’s why I fell in love with the name Daisy Chain. It served as a reminder of how individual parts can come together to create something strong and unbreakable.” THR
